messages:
sam: hey team, first-week onboarding question. I built the runtime from source inside the dev container but one of the unit tests keeps segfaulting when exercising the kv-cache. build succeeds and image starts, but test crashes. stack snippet below:

sam: ```
$ ./bazel-bin/runtime/tests/kv_cache_test --gtest_filter=KVCache.*
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
#0  0x7f8b2d4e1a in ?? () from /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcudart.so.12.0
#1  0x55a3b6c3f4 in runtime::kv::Store::append(...)
#2  0x55a3b6c8a1 in main
```

sam: I also did a quick strace and see several dlopen attempts failing for libnvidia-ml.so.1

mika: did you build against the same CUDA/toolkit version that's on the node? which cuda_toolchain value are you using in bazel? :thinking:

sam: using the default dev container from devex (cuda:12.2-base). `nvidia-smi` on the node shows driver 535.86 and CUDA 12.2:

sam: ```
$ nvidia-smi
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 535.86       Driver Version: 535.86       CUDA Version: 12.2     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

tiago: try `ldd` on the shared object to confirm missing symlinks. we often see libnvidia-ml not mounted into the container even when the host has working drivers.

sam: ldd output for the runtime shared lib shows:

sam: ```
$ ldd bazel-bin/runtime/libredwood_runtime.so | grep nvidia
libnvidia-ml.so.1 => not found
libcuda.so.1 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 (0x00007f8b2c900000)
```

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-472: "kv-cache segfault on dev container - libnvidia-ml missing" and assigned to infra oncall. More details: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-472 :ticket:

olivia: quick local workaround: if you have a specific libnvidia-ml file in the container, create the expected symlink. e.g.: `sudo ln -s /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.535.86 /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.1` then re-run tests. on k8s ask infra to mount /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu from the node into the pod with driver libs.

sam: tried symlink hack, ldd now shows resolution but test still segfaults; new backtrace references nvml:

sam: ```
#0  0x7fffa1b2e3 in nvmlDeviceGetHandleByIndex_v2 () from /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.1
#1  0x55a3b6c3f4 in runtime::gpu::DeviceTracker::init()
#2  0x55a3b6c8a1 in runtime::kv::Store::append
```

mika: that could be an ABI/driver mismatch or our code calling NVML too early before gpu subsystem fully initialized. two quick checks: 1) run under gdb with `export CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` to get a reliable backtrace; 2) try the same image on a node with driver 535.* that matches the lib version, or rebuild the container with the driver-matching libnvidia-ml.

tiago: also check if the test spawns threads that touch NVML during static init; search for any gpu::DeviceTracker calls in test setup. sometimes a ctor runs before main and hits NVML. grep tests for DeviceTracker or global singletons.

sam: good point — will grep the test harness and run under gdb. if infra can repro with a driver mount that might speed up the fix. thanks for the pointers :thumbsup:
